expectations.text: Both skill and agent created (a pair)
expectations.evidence: Outputs tree contains exactly the two artifacts: .agents/skills/pkg-scout/SKILL.md and .omp/agent/agents/pkg-scout.md, both with complete frontmatter and substantial bodies. Linked as a pair: the skill's workflow step 2 says 'Delegate the legwork to the `pkg-scout` agent' with a ready-made task brief, and the agent's autoloadSkills references the same skill with a skill://pkg-scout re-read fallback.

expectations.text: Skill covers license, maintenance, last release, red flags
expectations.evidence: SKILL.md covers all four operationally: license compatibility ('Cite the SPDX id from the latest manifest', HIGH flag for absent/incompatible license, MEDIUM for version-range license flip); maintenance ('Publish timeline', cadence collapse, maintainer turnover/bus factor); last release ('npm view <pkg> time --json', 'No publish in >=18 months'); red flags as a severity-graded catalog (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW: deprecation, install lifecycle scripts, typosquat shape, hijack patterns like event-stream/ua-parser-js). Report template has dedicated License/Maintenance/Red flags sections.

expectations.text: Agent tools are omp-appropriate (web_search/read), no leftovers
expectations.evidence: Agent frontmatter: 'tools: read, grep, glob, bash, web_search'. No write/edit/task leftovers — the transcript states these are 'deliberately omitted, so it's read-only and cannot spawn children'. The extras are load-bearing, not template residue: bash runs the entire data-source table (npm view, curl registry/downloads/GitHub API, tarball listing without install), grep/glob support the 'read its package.json for the intended version range' context step. web_search and read are both present. Caveat: the assertion's '(web_search/read)' parenthetical reads like an exhaustive pair, so this passes only under the 'no mutating/spawning leftovers' reading — flagged in eval_feedback.

expectations.text: Agent has one-job statement and anti-jobs
expectations.evidence: One-job statement: 'You are **pkg-scout**, a read-only npm package vetting worker... You produce evidence-backed adoption reports and nothing else.' Anti-jobs are an explicit Hard rules block: 'You never edit files, never run `npm install` or `npx`, and never execute code from the package or its tarball.' plus 'never retry-spam' on rate limits, 'A failed fetch or missing field is `[UNKNOWN — reason]`, never a guess', and 'do not block on questions (you have no peer channel)'.

Description opens with the full capability list ('license, maintenance and release cadence, downloads trend, repo health, install-script and supply-chain red flags, alternatives') then enumerates trigger framings: 'Use whenever the user is about to adopt or choose an npm package, asks whether a package is maintained, safe, or trustworthy, asks to vet, audit, deep-dive, or evaluate a dependency, asks about a package's license or maintainers, or compares npm packages as candidates — even if they never say "vet" or "scout".' The 'even if they never say' clause is maximally pushy.

expectations.text: Skill spells out the task-tool delegation contract
expectations.evidence: Workflow step 2 embeds a concrete task-tool JSON brief showing every field: `context` ('Shared use case and constraints'), `tasks[]` with `agent: "pkg-scout"`, `task` ('Vet npm package <name>[@<version>]... Context: <...>'), `solutionSpace`; plus batching rule 'One task per package, all packages in a single batch (parallel)' and a fallback: 'If `pkg-scout` is not in the task tool's agent list... run the procedure below inline instead.'

claims.claim: Both frontmatters parsed with pyYAML (name, description present as strings; agent has tools + autoloadSkills)
claims.evidence: Transcript shows a bash pyYAML sanity-check step ran successfully ('ok · 3 lines'); inspection of both files confirms valid YAML frontmatter with string name/description and agent tools + autoloadSkills.

claims.claim: Names avoid collision with the bundled `scout` agent (exact-name, case-sensitive dedup)
claims.evidence: Agent is named pkg-scout, distinct from omp's bundled scout agent.

claims.claim: tools deliberately omit edit/write/task so the agent is read-only and cannot spawn children
claims.evidence: Agent frontmatter lists only read, grep, glob, bash, web_search; no write/edit/task keys.

claims.claim: Report template intentionally exists in both files (agent must be self-contained); keep in sync when editing
claims.evidence: Identical report template appears in SKILL.md ('### Report template') and in the agent body's 'Output contract' section.

claims.claim: autoloadSkills: [pkg-scout] — omp injects the skill into the agent's context before its first prompt
claims.evidence: Unverifiable from outputs: whether omp accepts YAML list syntax for autoloadSkills (the agent-craft template convention is CSV) and whether injection actually occurs cannot be checked without a live harness. Per grading instructions this syntax was explicitly out of scope — no assertion covers autoloadSkills, so it does not affect any verdict; flagged only as a claim.

needs_review: Baseline's suggested checks for Main (omp skill list / agents roster showing pkg-scout) were not run by the executor and remain open

suggestions.assertion: Skill covers license, maintenance, last release, red flags
suggestions.reason: Non-discriminating: the eval prompt itself enumerates 'license, maintenance, last release, red flags' verbatim, so echoing the request passes. A depth check (e.g. 'red-flag guidance distinguishes severity tiers' or 'each area names at least one concrete check/data source') would separate thin copies from real methodology.

suggestions.assertion: Agent tools are omp-appropriate (web_search/read), no leftovers
suggestions.reason: Ambiguous as written: the baseline passed with five tools (read, grep, glob, bash, web_search) because its extras are load-bearing and read-only, while the parenthetical reads like an exhaustive allow-list that the baseline fails. State the rule explicitly (e.g. 'must include web_search+read; must omit write/edit/task; other read-only tools allowed if the body uses them') or the assertion cannot arbitrate between toolset philosophies.

No assertion checks pair linkage/integrity — that the skill delegates to an agent name that actually exists at the user-level path (~/.omp/agent/agents/) and the skill sits at ~/.agents/skills/. A typo'd or dangling agent reference (or an autoloadSkills entry omp rejects) is the most likely real-world failure and went unchecked.

No assertion exercises the delegation contract end-to-end (e.g. dry-run one task-tool spawn using the skill's own field guidance, or verify the agent's output format matches what the skill promises the user). Both runs 'spell out' contracts that were never executed.

eval_feedback.overall: All six assertions are presence checks that both runs satisfy (6/6 here), so the eval cannot discriminate skill-following from competent improvisation — the baseline scored identically without reading agent-craft. Add content-depth, linkage, and one behavioral check.
